title: The buy-back step has no published operation for its case move, its deviation raise, its approval or its template read, gives no limit value and no field that holds the template price, and the buy-back has no value in the two closed lists
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-032, its Story, Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC3, Data, Endpoints, Screen and states, Permission checks and Validation and messages tables); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.23.1 to A2.23.4, FEAT-AST-23, rules VR-S5-023-1, R-DIS-66, BR-S5-023, field catalog, roles); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.0, T3.1 asset, listing and asset_sale, T3.2 LOV-LISTING, LOV-SALE-CHANNEL, LOV-HOLDING, T4, T6.1, appendix T-A.1); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-24, R-DIS-61, R-DIS-62, R-DIS-66, R-DIS-68, state table); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (FEAT-AST-23 row, systems AMIS, ALS and GL); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 (REQ-S5-010); _work/msr/context/S5.md (service row, ownership rows of S5, DP table short form); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (both slices of RWB-E4-032, C list empty, reqs empty)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 1, 3, 4, 7; s5 Exception paths; s8 Business rules; s9 State transitions; s10 Authority; s11 Data; s12.2; s12.5; s13 Solution plan; s15 Screens and states; s18 Traceability
description: The legacy story gives the buy-back one screen action and refers the rest to the module: AC1 says only that the user acts on the screen, and the two endpoints it lists are one asset read and one listing write under the old monolith base, with no buy-back operation of any kind. The rules that govern the feature are R-DIS-24 (agree the buy-back terms at the template price, when route = buy_back and second_signature given) and R-DIS-66, and neither the FSD nor the rule set publishes the operation that applies a case move on behalf of a stage, the operation that raises the deviation, the cost of the approval child or the read of the template. The limit behind second_signature is a delegated-authority row; no source gives a value, a currency or a unit for it, and the row itself is rwb-access's. The template price of R-DIS-24 has no field: the FSD field catalog of A2.23 lists eight ACE asset fields only, the legacy Data table names decision_log_entry, deviation, assignment and two ACE views, and neither the physical schema nor the data model gives listing or asset_sale a template or price-version column, so which of floor_price and sale_price carries the value, and whether a third row is needed, is unsettled. The buy-back also has no value in the closed lists the element must use: LOV-SALE-CHANNEL gives DUTCH_AUCTION, BROKER, DIRECT, LED_AUCTION and RAMC and LOV-LISTING gives DRAFT, LIVE, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD and WITHDRAWN, so neither a buy-back channel nor a buy-back listing status exists and no value is invented. The plan's reqs list of the slice is empty while REQ-S5-010 (a transfer to the asset management company, a buy-back and a rental each follow a recorded approval) names exactly the outcome of AC1. Each unnamed value carries the placeholder of Template and Rules v1 R9 and is settled at the baseline review.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-032 lists GET /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId} and POST /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId}/listings only, and its AC1 gives no from state; FSD S5 A2.23.3.1 tables VR-S5-023-1, R-DIS-66 and BR-S5-023 only, and its A2.23.3.2 field catalog holds eight v_ace_* fields; TSD S5 T3.1 gives listing eight and asset_sale eleven business columns, none named for a template or a price version; TSD S5 T3.2 gives the five channel and five listing values named above; the split plan gives reqs as an empty list for RWB-S5-E4032-APP; Business Requirements Program v4 gives REQ-S5-010 for the buy-back approval.
area: Contract, data model and list values, S5 rwb-asset
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the data steward, the P7 rwb-decision owner and the P4 rwb-access owner
proposed: Keep listing and asset_sale as the only rows, declare the case-move answer, the deviation raise and the template read on their owners' contracts with placeholders, treat the limit as a delegated-authority row read at its version, let the contract baseline decide which of floor_price and sale_price holds the template price, and let step D1 add REQ-S5-010 to the reqs list of both slices.

title: The contract baseline of the buy-back slice has no published payload for the approval answer or the deviation reference, no published name for four of the five consumed rows, and no buy-back value in LOV-SALE-CHANNEL or LOV-LISTING
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.23.2 integration points AMIS, ALS and GL; A2.23.3.1 rules; A2.23.3.3 roles); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1 asset, listing, asset_sale; T3.2 lists; T3.3 relationships; T6.1 rights matrix; T-A.1 endpoint inventory; T-A.2 API-S5-001 and API-S5-002); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-24, R-DIS-61, R-DIS-62, R-DIS-66); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-032 Data and Validation and messages tables); _work/msr/context/S5.md (service row, six REST operations, one event, one job, one workflow, DP table short form); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (patterns DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19; C and X lists empty)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s5 Exception paths; s7 AC2, AC3, AC4; s8 Business rules; s11 Data; s12.2; s12.8; s13 Solution plan; s15 Screens and states; s18 Traceability
description: The baseline has to declare five consumed rows and can name only one of them: the case read is published as GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}, while the case-move answer, the deviation raise, the approval child and the template read have no published operation name, request shape or answer shape in any source read by this work package. The approval answer in particular has no element: the maker-checker kit takes the DoA lookup as a parameter and returns an answer, but no field list exists, so approved, approver role, limit reference and answer date are declared as fields of the baseline with the placeholder and are not taken from a document. The deviation reference is the same: rwb-deviation owns the record and the pause, and no published element for a raise answer exists. The two written rows bring their own two list defects, because LOV-SALE-CHANNEL and LOV-LISTING have no buy-back value, so the element must carry the placeholder rather than a new list member. The baseline also has to stay silent on two things the sources leave open elsewhere: no field may need a v_ace_* grant (DP-05 is a prohibition in this slice, and the legacy v_ace_customer and v_ace_npa_sale rows are the former owner and the NPA sale facts, both rwb-source-data's), and the decision record is the platform library's element, never a local copy (DP-03).
evidence: TSD S5 T-A.1 publishes five operations of the service, all of them its own; no appendix, no OpenAPI and no AsyncAPI in the extract set gives a shape for the case-move answer, the deviation raise, the approval child or the template read; the FSD integration points name AMIS, ALS and GL, which are outside the Workbench and belong to rwb-integration and rwb-payment; LOV-SALE-CHANNEL and LOV-LISTING hold the five values each and no buy-back value; the split plan gives the two slices an empty C and X list, so no other service contract is named for the buy-back.
area: Contract baseline and payload shapes, S5 rwb-asset
owner_role: Solution architect of S5 rwb-asset with the S8 rwb-deviation, P7 rwb-decision and P6 rwb-comms contract owners
proposed: Publish the two reads with the buy-back element, declare the four unnamed consumed rows with a placeholder and a 2 s timeout, reference the platform decision-record element, keep the lists unchanged with a placeholder for the buy-back value, and tag baseline v1 before the application story builds.

title: Legacy AC1 gives no from state while R-DIS-24 starts at ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER, and the criterion's screen action has no state of its own
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-032: AC1 Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place / When the user acts on the screen; AC2 Given a case in state ASSET_HELD); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-24 from ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER, R-DIS-66 from ASSET_HELD, R-DIS-27 refusal to ASSET_HELD); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T4 DISPOSAL state table, rows R-DIS-24 and R-DIS-25)
section: APP s5 Exception paths; s8 Business rules; s9 State transitions; s18 Traceability; CON s9 State transitions
description: The two sources of the feature disagree on the state the buy-back starts from. Legacy AC1 states only that the data and the rule version are in place and that the user acts on the screen, while AC2 of the same story is precise (a case in state ASSET_HELD). The rule set makes R-DIS-24 a transition from ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER on ROUTE_APPROVED with route = buy_back and second_signature given, and the TSD state table repeats it. The higher source in the precedence list is the rule set, so the story reads AC1 with the from state ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER and adds no state to the criterion itself. The refusal path is the third state fact no source settles for this feature: R-DIS-27 returns the asset to hold on approver_decision = refused and belongs to the route-approval slice, so the buy-back step writes nothing on a refusal and the criterion stays silent about it.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-032 AC1 Given line names no state; AC2 names ASSET_HELD; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 gives R-DIS-24 from ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER to ROUTE_APPROVED_BUYBACK and R-DIS-27 from ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER to ASSET_HELD on a refusal; TSD S5 T4 repeats both transitions.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the P3 rwb-case owner and the business analyst of module S5
proposed: Read AC1 with the from state ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER of R-DIS-24, keep the criterion word for word, and let the route-approval slice own the refusal of R-DIS-27.

title: The FSD rule list of A2.23 omits R-DIS-24, which the rule set assigns to the buy-back route, so the module document and the rule set disagree on the rules of the feature
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.23.3.1: VR-S5-023-1, R-DIS-66, BR-S5-023 only); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-24 route = buy_back, R-DIS-61 and R-DIS-62 from ROUTE_APPROVED_BUYBACK); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T4 row R-DIS-24); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-032 AC1, approval the limit requires)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s8 Business rules; s18 Traceability
description: The functional specification of module S5 tables three rules for FEAT-AST-23: VR-S5-023-1 (floor price below the approver's limit), R-DIS-66 (the deviation pause) and BR-S5-023 (no business value in code). It does not table R-DIS-24, the rule that agrees the buy-back terms at the template price once the second signature is given, although the rule set and the TSD state table both give R-DIS-24 the buy-back route as its condition and AC1 of the legacy story turns on that signature. The rule set is the source of the rule and the FSD is a narrative document, so the story uses R-DIS-24 and records the omission; the FSD's rule list is not edited, because every source is read-only in this run. The two completion rules R-DIS-61 and R-DIS-62 are tabled for context only, because they start where this slice ends.
evidence: FSD S5 A2.23.3.1 tables VR-S5-023-1, R-DIS-66 and BR-S5-023; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 gives R-DIS-24 with the condition route = buy_back and second_signature given; TSD S5 T4 repeats the same transition; legacy AC1 names the approval the limit requires.
owner_role: Business analyst of module S5 with the P7 rwb-decision rule owner
proposed: Keep R-DIS-24 as the rule of the buy-back step, table it in the story with its source, and correct the FSD rule list of A2.23 in the next FSD version after the verification loop.

title: The FSD gives the customer (borrower) as an also-user of the buy-back while the rights matrix has no customer role
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.23.3.3 Roles and permissions: Sale officer primary, Head of NPA and Customer (borrower) also use); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T6.1 RBAC matrix, 31 rows, no customer role); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-032 Permission checks table)
section: APP s10 Authority; CON s10 Authority
description: The role table of FEAT-AST-23 names the customer (borrower) as an also-user of the buy-back, and the rights matrix of the service has no customer role at all: its 31 rows are Workbench staff roles, partner roles and service identities. The legacy permission checks table likewise holds Workbench roles only. The customer is therefore a party of the case and not a Workbench user in the target, and the story grants no right to it. What a customer may see or sign is a portal question and belongs to the partner gateway and rwb-partner (S9), which this slice does not reach.
evidence: FSD S5 A2.23.3.3 lists Customer (borrower) as also-user; TSD S5 T6.1 has no customer row; the legacy permission checks table of RWB-E4-032 names RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-FIELDCOL, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-LEGAL, RW-SALEOFF, RW-NPAMGR and SY-DATALOAD only.
owner_role: P4 rwb-access owner with the business analyst of module S5
proposed: Treat the customer as a party of the case and not as a Workbench role, grant no right to it in this slice, and record the portal question with the P4 and S9 owners.
